verdicts.strongest_argument: The claim is contradicted by its own price bars, and its evidence is published in the corpus. The 97.94%-calls datapoint is an automated flow-bot post on a public StockTwits feed, captured verbatim in docs/50e5afee...txt at 2026-08-29T05:18:47Z, alongside 'Largest CALL OI Increases $NVDA $AI ...' on 2026-08-27T13:12:12Z and again on 2026-08-31T13:57:25Z in docs/2e374643...txt. So the aggregation the hunter says 'nobody does' is literally in the captured feed, twice, on consecutive sweeps. Worse, the hunter's own logic inverts the tape: it argues that if the crowding were priced the stock would not have risen 8.45%, but quote.json shows 08-26 close 9.70 -> 08-27 10.33 (+6.5% on 5.14m shares) -> 08-31 10.82 (6.44m shares vs a 4.67m 20d average). The rally and the volume build land on exactly the sessions the call flow is dated to. A price that has already gone up 11.5% in four sessions on above-average volume, with the corpus carrying a 2026-08-27 post reading 'starting to wake up + run up into earnings call', is the crowding expressed in the price, not evidence it is unexpressed. What remains unpriced is at most the second-order point that a 35%-of-float short base plus one-sided calls widens the tails - but the hunter itself calls the band 'deliberately wide and two-sided', which is a statement about variance, not a signed edge, and a variance statement cannot be ranked against a directional one. I withhold the last 20 points only because the corpus has no options chain, so I cannot verify whether dealer positioning was more extreme than the price move implies.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Public StockTwits post dated 2026-08-29T05:18:47Z states 152.49K AI options traded on August 28, 2.06% puts and 97.94% calls - the exact datapoint the finding rests on.
Feed carries 'Largest CALL OI Increases $NVDA $AI $KHC $HONA $RXT' on 2026-08-27, i.e. the OI-increase screen the finding cites is itself a published, syndicated list.
Same call-OI-increase screen names $AI again on 2026-08-31, one session before the print.
DA Davidson Underperform, $7 target, published 2026-09-01 - the bearish counterweight is also already public.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json (fetched 2026-09-02T15:07Z; the 09-02 bar is a partial intraday bar at 1.00m shares and I did not use it for anything but noting spot). Run-up 5d +8.45% and 20d +6.16% per the baseline, with the specific up-days 08-27 (+6.5%) and 08-31 (+4.7%) carrying 5.14m and 6.44m shares against a 4.67m 20d average - volume built on precisely the dates the cited call flow is dated. Reaction history is 6 down of 8 with an 8.49% median, so the tails the finding points at are already the baseline's own expected move; it is not adding magnitude.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: An options chain or dealer-gamma series showing call open interest at a level the 11.5% four-session rally does not already account for, or evidence the flow post-dated the price move rather than coinciding with it.

interactions: Single claim; internally the finding cites both the bullish flow cluster and a bearish DA Davidson note from the same corpus, which is why its own stated band is two-sided and unrankable.
corpus_limits: No options chain is recoverable retrospectively, so I cannot test the size of the call open interest against the realised rally directly - only the coincidence of dates. The AI capture carries no wire copy, previews or sell-side previews beyond the price-target doc, so the claim that 'the wire copy is consensus EPS and the AI-adoption story' is untestable here: that absence is a capture artefact. quote.json has no 2026-08-28 bar at all, so I could not measure the move on the exact day of the cited flow.
